report.headline: Projected usage falls from 26.6% in the EuroLeague to 19.9% in the NBA, essentially at the league-average 20.1%, while the true-shooting projection carries no real information because it fails to beat a trivial baseline.

projection.text: The model projects a 19.9% NBA usage rate, down from a 26.6% EuroLeague usage rate, landing almost exactly at the 20.1% minutes-weighted average usage rate for qualified NBA players in the target season.

risks.text: A 16.8% turnover rate combined with heavy reliance on threes (56.8% of attempts) could compress efficiency against tougher, faster NBA defenses.
The true shooting projection should not be relied upon: its 4.7% error is no better than the 4.7% error of the trivial league-mean baseline.
The source-season sample is limited to 970 minutes over 31 games at age 28, a thin and late-career base from which to extrapolate a role change.

The historical EL->NBA cohort behind this estimate numbers only 61 transitions, and those movers sat just 0.46 sd above their own league average on entry — well below this player's 1.26 sd standing — so the fitted 0.58 usage slope may understate how much of his advantage carries over.

strengths.text: Averaged 6.162 assists per 75 possessions and a 29.3% assist rate in the EuroLeague, with usage sitting 1.26 standard deviations above league average, indicating a ball-dominant, high-usage role in the source season.
Posted a 59.1% true shooting percentage in the source season, almost exactly at the EuroLeague average (+0.01 sd), suggesting efficient scoring for his role at the time.
The usage-rate projection model beats the trivial league-mean baseline (3.3% vs 4.3% mean absolute error over 367 held-out transitions), giving some grounding to the usage number specifically.

uncertainty.text: The 80% prediction interval for usage runs from 14.2% to 25.5% — an 11.3-point span, roughly two standard deviations of the 5.6% NBA usage spread — so the model can rank this transition but not price an individual outcome; the true shooting projection of 56.3% is even less trustworthy, since the model's 4.7% mean absolute error is no better than the 4.7% error of simply guessing the league-mean true shooting figure.
